pemmican:moddesc: Smoke meat into jerky, grind it to powder, and render it with fat into long-lasting pemmican.
item-handbooktext-smashingrock: A crude stone knapped into a crushing tool. Use it in the crafting grid to grind jerky into jerky powder. It wears out with use. See the Pemmican guide.
_comment-meal-names: Cooking-pot meal names are looked up by vanilla in the game domain (unqualified), so these must be game: prefixed. meal-<code> is the shortcut that names it regardless of serving size.
_comment-stew-ingredient: Jerky's name as a stew ingredient (e.g. 'Jerky stew'). VS falls back to the first code part, so one key covers all jerky-<type> variants.
_comment-handbook-ingredients: Handbook 'Required Ingredients' labels, keyed by each cooking-recipe ingredient's typeName.
smokerack-needfire: Smoking paused — the fire is out.
smokingfirepit-firepitbusy: Empty the firepit before fitting the rack.
guide-pemmican-text:
Pemmican & jerky
Trail food that keeps for months.

Preserving meat takes three steps: smoke it into jerky, grind the jerky into powder, then cook the powder with fat into pemmican.

1. Dry or smoke meat into jerky
Craft a drying rack from 3 sticks, a rope and a knife. Right-click it with raw redmeat, bushmeat, fish or poultry to hang up to 8 pieces — aim at a spot to fill it, or hold Ctrl to hang a whole stack. There are two ways to dry:

Air-dry — place the rack on the ground. It dries slowly from the weather: quickest in warm, sunny, dry air, paused and set back by rain, and racing against spoilage in the cold or damp. A cellar dries slowly but holds rot at bay.

Smoke — right-click an empty firepit with the rack to fit it over the fire, turning it into a smoking rack. Feed it firewood or peat (one piece per click), light it with a torch or firestarter, and it smokes low and slow — about a day per batch, fast and reliable in any weather. Empty the rack and right-click it empty-handed to pop it back off, leaving a plain firepit.

Either way, empty-handed you can take pieces off (aim at one, or Ctrl to grab them all). Jerky keeps for months — far longer than fresh or cooked meat — and can be eaten as-is or added to stews.

2. Grind jerky into powder
Grind jerky in a quern, or crush it in the crafting grid with a smashing rock (knapped from stone). Each meat keeps its own nutrition, so redmeat jerky yields redmeat jerky powder, and so on.

3. Cook pemmican
In a cooking pot over a firepit, combine 1 rendered fat with 1 to 3 jerky powder to make pemmican — a dense, portable protein meal. Add a measure of salt to make salted pemmican, which keeps roughly twice as long. Serve it into bowls, or seal it in a crock to preserve it even further.
block-handbooktext-smokerack: A rack for drying meat and fruit, hanging up to 8 pieces. Place it on the ground (even in a cellar) to slowly air-dry — faster in warm, sunny, dry weather, stalled or set back by rain, and racing against spoilage in cold or damp conditions. Or right-click an empty firepit with it to fit it over the fire and smoke instead, which is much faster and works in any weather. Break it to take it back. See the Pemmican guide.
block-handbooktext-smokingfirepit-*: A drying rack fitted over a firepit, forming a smoking rack. Feed it firewood or peat, light it, and hang up to 8 pieces of meat to slow-smoke them into jerky (Ctrl-click hangs or grabs a whole stack at once) — much faster and more reliable than air-drying. Empty the rack and right-click empty-handed to take the rack back, leaving a plain firepit. See the Pemmican guide.
item-handbooktext-jerky-*: Smoked, dried meat that keeps for months. Eat it as-is, add it to stews, or grind it into jerky powder for making pemmican. See the Pemmican guide.
item-handbooktext-jerkypowder-*: Ground jerky that keeps the nutrition of its source meat. Cook it with rendered fat in a pot to make pemmican. See the Pemmican guide.
